skill.name: xss-html-injection
skill.description: Assess authorized web applications for stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS and HTML injection vulnerabilities with structured testing and remediation guidance.
skill.summary: Identify client-side injection flaws and document practical remediation in authorized environments.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: The skill is an offensive XSS testing guide with explicit authorization gates. It also supplies operational keylogging, session theft, phishing, and defense-evasion instructions that create critical misuse risk. Syntax inventories, Markdown fences, placeholder targets, and defensive limitations were dismissed as false positives.

remediation.issue: Operational payloads capture keystrokes, cookies, local storage, and credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Replace data-capture payloads with inert markers that demonstrate execution without collecting or transmitting sensitive information.

remediation.issue: Examples send captured data to attacker-controlled placeholder domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use a local lab endpoint and require dummy data, disposable sessions, and explicit confirmation before any network request.

remediation.issue: The guide explains phishing delivery, interface impersonation, and security-control bypasses.
remediation.suggestion: Remove delivery and impersonation instructions. Limit bypass examples to defensive analysis in isolated training applications.

remediation.issue: The guardrails rely on user confirmation but cannot technically constrain payload execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require localhost or an approved lab allowlist and prohibit production testing, credential collection, persistence, and third-party targeting.

content.value_statement: Client-side injection flaws can expose user sessions and alter trusted pages. This skill structures authorized XSS discovery, validation, classification, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Maps user-controlled inputs to browser rendering contexts and dangerous DOM sinks.
Tests stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS behavior in authorized environments.
Explains HTML injection, context-specific payload construction, and encoding variations.
Evaluates sanitization, output encoding, cookie protections, and Content Security Policy behavior.
Produces vulnerability evidence, severity classifications, and remediation recommendations.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a clearly defined target scope before active testing.
Cannot guarantee coverage of framework-specific sanitizers, browser differences, or custom application logic.
Content Security Policy, HttpOnly cookies, and modern auto-escaping can limit demonstrations.
Includes offensive examples that must remain within isolated labs or explicitly authorized assessments.

use_cases.title: Validate a Web Release
use_cases.description: Review new input and rendering paths for stored, reflected, and DOM-based injection before deployment.

use_cases.title: Reproduce an XSS Report
use_cases.description: Confirm a reported issue with a non-destructive proof and document its source, sink, context, and impact.

use_cases.title: Improve Output Handling
use_cases.description: Compare vulnerable rendering behavior with suitable encoding, sanitization, and browser security controls.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Rendering Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized rendering pattern for XSS risk. Identify the source, sink, output context, and a safe remediation. Do not provide data-theft payloads.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe XSS Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a non-destructive XSS test plan for [authorized target]. Cover stored, reflected, and DOM paths using alert-only or inert markers.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Sanitization Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess how [application flow] handles untrusted input across HTML, attributes, URLs, JavaScript, and CSS. Recommend context-specific encoding and sanitization.

prompt_templates.title: Design an End-to-End Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized XSS assessment for [scope]. Include prerequisites, source-to-sink tracing, safe validation, CSP review, evidence standards, severity, and remediation tests.

output_examples.input: Review a search page that writes the query into a results heading.
output_examples.output: The query reaches an HTML context without verified encoding. Test with an inert marker, inspect the DOM, and apply context-aware output encoding.

output_examples.input: Assess a profile biography saved and displayed to other users.
output: Classify the path as a stored injection candidate.
Use a harmless unique marker in a test account.
Check server sanitization and final browser DOM.
Recommend allowlist sanitization and output encoding.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a page that inserts location.hash through innerHTML.
output_examples.output: This is a DOM-XSS path because attacker-controlled fragment data reaches an HTML sink. Replace innerHTML with textContent or sanitize trusted markup.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, exact targets, allowed techniques, test accounts, and data-handling rules before active testing.
Prefer inert markers and alert-only proofs that demonstrate execution without collecting credentials, cookies, or personal data.
Document each source, transformation, sink, browser context, observed effect, and verified remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not test production users, third-party systems, or targets outside the confirmed scope.
Do not collect credentials, session tokens, keystrokes, or other sensitive data for demonstration.
Do not distribute crafted links, bypass controls for persistence, or use payloads that affect unintended users.

faq.question: Does this skill require authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. Active testing requires written permission, an exact target, defined scope, and explicit confirmation before commands or payloads are used.

faq.question: Which XSS types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS, plus related HTML injection and browser rendering contexts.

faq.question: Can it test production systems?
faq.answer: Use isolated labs whenever possible. Production testing requires explicit approval, strict limits, test accounts, and an agreed incident plan.

faq.question: Does it replace automated scanners?
faq.answer: No. It guides manual reasoning and validation, while scanners provide broader automated coverage and repeatable regression checks.

faq.question: What evidence should a report include?
faq.answer: Include the input source, rendering sink, context, harmless proof, affected users, security controls, impact, and verified remediation.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Avoid collecting it. Use dummy accounts and synthetic values, then follow the approved data-handling and deletion requirements.
